newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai, Renault in Malaysian auto venture.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai, Renault in Malaysian auto venture.

text.p: Hyundai Motor Co Ltd, South Korea's biggest car maker, said on Tuesday it would build a vehicle plant in Malaysia in a joint venture with Renault of France.
A Hyundai official said the venture, which was aimed at producing 20,000 commercial vehicles a year, also involved the Malaysian government and companies. He declined to give the size of the venture.
The official said contracts would be formally signed on September 6 and production would begin in the second half of 1997.
Hyundai and Renault would each hold a 15 percent stake in the venture, while the Malaysian government and companies would have the remaining 70 percent.
The official said the venture would produce Renault's mid-sized buses late next year and Hyundai's small trucks from 1998.
He said truck production would increase from 1,500 units in 1998 to 7,000 units by 2000.
